tasks.title: Implement StageWorker orchestration glue in ngv2/workers/base.py
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/workers/base.py defines a callable StageWorker(task, get_task_fn, stage_fn, write_fn).
StageWorker calls get_task_fn(task) exactly once to obtain the context before any staging or writing.
StageWorker passes the fetched context to stage_fn and collects the returned artifact dict(s).
Each artifact dict returned by stage_fn is written to the task's output_path via write_fn.
A stage_fn return of a single dict and a return of a list of dicts are both handled, with each dict written once.
An empty artifact result causes zero write_fn calls and StageWorker still completes without error.
Call ordering get_task_fn -> stage_fn -> write_fn is preserved and a missing output_path raises a clear error.
Module does NOT define build_default_seams, the conductor loop, gated_advance, get_task, or any phase worker.

spec.objective: Provide the base worker orchestration primitive StageWorker that wires a task fetch, a staging step, and an artifact write into a single deterministic pipeline, with all collaborators injected so no concrete seam, conductor, get_task, or phase-worker logic is built here.
functional_requirements: Expose a callable StageWorker(task, get_task_fn, stage_fn, write_fn) from ngv2/workers/base.py.
Fetch the working context by invoking get_task_fn(task) and use its return value as the context fed downstream.
Run stage_fn over the fetched context to produce the structured artifact result.
Write each artifact dict returned by stage_fn to the task's output_path via write_fn.
Normalize the stage_fn return so a single dict and a list of dicts are both written one artifact at a time.
Preserve the invocation ordering get_task_fn before stage_fn before write_fn and surface a clear error when output_path is absent.
spec.interfaces: StageWorker(task, get_task_fn, stage_fn, write_fn) -> list of written artifact dicts. get_task_fn(session_row: dict) -> {phase, target, prior_findings, parked_package} (injected, conductor_glue/ngv2.session_get_task). stage_fn(context) -> dict | list[dict] (injected, e.g. a run_stage(context, seams) already bound to its seams). write_fn(output_path, artifact: dict) -> None (injected sink).
edge_cases: stage_fn returns an empty list: write_fn is never called and StageWorker returns an empty collection.
stage_fn returns a single bare dict rather than a list: it is wrapped and written exactly once.
stage_fn returns multiple dicts: write_fn is called once per dict, in order.
task is missing output_path: StageWorker raises a clear KeyError/ValueError before any write occurs.
get_task_fn raises: the exception propagates and neither stage_fn nor write_fn is invoked.
non_goals: Do not build build_default_seams or any seam assembly logic.
Do not implement the conductor loop or gated_advance.
Do not implement get_task (session_get_task.py); it is injected as get_task_fn.
Do not author any phase worker module (hunt, triage, verify, poc, detonate, novelty, report).
spec.implementation_notes:
Do NOT create ngv2/workers/__init__.py -- ngv2/workers is a namespace package; sibling workers (detonate.py, novelty.py, report.py) ship with NO __init__.py. An empty/non-mergeable __init__.py is what made this leaf fail AST-merge (incomplete_ast@L0). Build ONLY the named .py module(s).

Keep StageWorker dependency-free and side-effect-only through the injected write_fn. Read output_path from the task argument. Treat stage_fn's contract as dict|list[dict] and normalize via isinstance check. Do not import session_get_task or any seam/conductor module at runtime; collaborators are passed in. Add a minimal ngv2/workers/__init__.py so the package imports cleanly.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Fake injected collaborators: a get_task_fn returning a context dict {phase, target, prior_findings, parked_package}; a stage_fn returning configurable dict / list[dict] / empty list; a recording write_fn that captures (output_path, artifact) tuples. Sample task dicts with and without output_path.

token_budget_ratio.note: Small focused glue module; the paired oracle (separate task) carries the heavier verification budget, so impl-side tests stay lean but still exceed implementation tokens per ratio.

tasks.title: Author paired mutation-tested oracle for ngv2/workers/base.py
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/workers/test_base.py is a sibling test file for ngv2/workers/base.py.
The oracle verifies StageWorker with at least two edge cases (empty artifact list and multi-dict return).
Tests use injected fakes for get_task_fn, stage_fn, and write_fn (no real session_get_task or seams).
The authored test FAILS against the declared mutant of ngv2.workers.base (non-vacuity).
verification_command names the authored oracle and runs green against the correct implementation.

spec.objective: Author the paired oracle that pins the StageWorker contract: fetch-via-get_task_fn, stage-over-context, write-each-artifact-to-output_path, exercising at least two edge cases and failing against a deliberate mutant of ngv2.workers.base.
functional_requirements: Assert StageWorker fetches context by calling get_task_fn(task) and feeds that context into stage_fn.
Assert every artifact dict returned by stage_fn is written to the task's output_path via write_fn, once each and in order.
Edge case one: a stage_fn returning an empty list yields zero write_fn calls.
Edge case two: a stage_fn returning multiple dicts (and a single bare dict) is written one artifact at a time.
Assert a task missing output_path raises before any write occurs (ordering/error edge case).
spec.interfaces: Imports StageWorker from ngv2.workers.base. Constructs fake get_task_fn(session_row)->context dict, fake stage_fn(context)->dict|list[dict], and a recording write_fn(output_path, artifact) capturing calls for assertions.
edge_cases: Multiple artifact dicts -> one write per dict in order.
Single bare dict return normalized to one write.
Missing output_path -> error raised before any write_fn call.
get_task_fn must be called exactly once and before stage_fn (mutant swapping order/skipping fetch must be caught).
non_goals: Do not test build_default_seams, the conductor loop, gated_advance, get_task, or any phase worker.
Do not exercise real filesystem or session collaborators; all are faked/injected.
spec.implementation_notes: Use a recording write_fn that appends (output_path, artifact) tuples and a call-order log shared across the fakes so ordering assertions catch a mutant that reorders or drops a step. Ensure at least one assertion is sensitive to the count of writes so the empty-list and multi-dict cases distinguish correct code from a mutant that always writes once or never writes. The mutation_target ngv2.workers.base's declared mutant must cause at least one test to fail.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Recording write_fn capturing (output_path, artifact); fake get_task_fn returning {phase, target, prior_findings, parked_package}; parametrized stage_fn returns covering empty list, single dict, and multi-dict; task fixtures with and without output_path; a shared call-order log to assert fetch->stage->write sequencing.

token_budget_ratio.note: test_authoring task: the deliverable is the oracle itself; budget weights the authored tests above the scaffolding/fakes implementation.
